description: Collaboration roadmap for SANDWICH v2 — from a messy brief to an execution-ready spec. See [`PRODUCT.md`](./PRODUCT.md) for product intent and [`README.md`](./README.md) for setup.

milestones.name: Versioning via git
milestones.goal: Replace the Postgres version snapshots with git operations on each project repository.

issues.title: Commit per generation
issues.what: After every successful generate / refine, stage the changed deliverable(s) + `BRIEF.md` and commit with a structured message (deliverable type + version, conversation id, prompt summary). Persist the resulting SHA to `documents.last_commit_sha`.
issues.why: The git log becomes the version history that the sidebar and rollback read from.
acceptance: Exactly one commit per successful run, app-authored, with metadata in the body
`last_commit_sha` updated on the affected `documents` rows
An empty diff produces no commit and a "nothing changed" reply
issues.notes: Commit via `child_process` inside the workspace module from M1-03.

issues.title: Rollback via git
issues.what: Rewire the existing rollback-intent parsing (`apps/server/prototype/rollback.ts`) to git: "rollback ke v2" resolves the Nth deliverable commit and restores that file, then commits the restore.
issues.why: The rollback UX already exists in chat; only the backing store changes.
acceptance: "rollback", "kembali ke versi sebelumnya", "v2" all resolve to git operations
Rollback creates a new commit — no history rewrite
Preview reflects the rolled-back file
issues.notes: Operate per deliverable file, not the whole tree.

issues.title: Version history + diff API
issues.what: Endpoints that return the `git log` for a deliverable (SHA, date, message, prompt summary) and a unified diff between two SHAs, for the sidebar version panel.
issues.why: PRODUCT.md §7 promises version history and per-prompt diffs in the sidebar.
acceptance: `GET /api/projects/:id/documents/:type/history`
`GET /api/projects/:id/documents/:type/diff?from=&to=` returns unified diff text
Both guarded by project ownership

milestones.name: Preview & retrieval from the filesystem
milestones.goal: Serve prototype previews and document content from disk (and from past commits) instead of Postgres.

issues.title: `/p` preview served from disk
issues.what: `/p/:projectId/` serves `prototype/index.html` from the project directory; `/p/:projectId/v/:sha/` serves that file at a past commit via `git show`. Keep the auth check.
issues.why: `document_files` is gone; the preview must read the on-disk file.
acceptance: Latest and versioned preview both work from disk
404 when no prototype file exists for the project
`prototypePreviewUrl` updated from `/p/:docId` to `/p/:projectId`

issues.title: Document read / download from disk
issues.what: Document content endpoints in `apps/server/routes/documents.ts` read the file from the project directory (optionally at a given SHA) instead of `document_versions`.
issues.why: Same reason — the version tables no longer exist.
acceptance: Get latest content, get content at a SHA, and download (.md / .html) all work
Every read goes through `resolveInsideProject`

issues.title: Project file-tree API for the sidebar
issues.what: `GET /api/projects/:id/files` returns the deliverables present on disk (type, filename, last commit, updated-at) to power the document panel.
issues.why: The sidebar now reflects a directory, not a set of `documents` rows with embedded content.
acceptance: Lists the known deliverables that exist on disk
`BRIEF.md`, `.git`, and any internal files are excluded or flagged internal

milestones.name: Durability & lifecycle
milestones.goal: Back the single-copy volume with R2, and handle project deletion and storage limits.

issues.title: R2 backup per project
issues.what: After each commit, asynchronously push a `git bundle` of the project repo to R2 under `projects/:userId/:projectId.bundle`.
issues.why: The Railway Volume is a single copy. R2 is the durability net and the escape hatch if we later change hosts or need to scale out.
acceptance: Bundle uploaded after each commit, non-blocking, retried on failure
Backup failures are logged and surfaced in metrics, never to the user

issues.title: Lazy-restore a project from R2
issues.what: When a project directory is requested but missing on disk (volume recreated, new host), restore it from its R2 bundle before use.
issues.why: Makes the volume disposable and keeps redeploys safe even if the volume is wiped.
acceptance: Missing dir + existing bundle → cloned from the bundle transparently
Missing dir + no bundle → treated as a new empty project
Restore is idempotent and locked per project

issues.title: Project deletion
issues.what: Deleting a project removes its DB rows (conversations, documents, chat_messages, attachment metadata), its on-disk directory, its R2 bundle, and its R2 attachment objects. Deleting a single conversation removes only that conversation + its Pi session, never the project.
issues.why: No orphaned disk or object storage.
acceptance: DB rows removed in one transaction; disk + R2 cleanup best-effort with logging
Deleting a conversation leaves the project and its other conversations intact

issues.title: Per-user disk guardrails
issues.what: Cap total project bytes per user (and per project), with a clear error when exceeded. Keep the existing monthly document / chat quotas.
issues.why: Filesystem storage per user is now effectively unbounded.
acceptance: Size check before a generate run writes files
Limits configurable per plan (Starter vs Pro)
Over-limit returns 403 with an actionable message

issues.title: Per-tenant isolation for engine tool execution
issues.what: Run each generation engine (esp. the prototype engine's bash tool) under real isolation — a per-user OS uid, a container, or a jailed filesystem — so a prompt-injected tool call cannot read another tenant's project directory under PROJECTS_ROOT.
issues.why: After M2-01 the engines run with cwd inside PROJECTS_ROOT and M2-02 feeds user-controlled attachment text into their context. Pi's tools resolve relative paths to cwd but pass absolute paths through — there is no sandbox. The env-scrub on bash and dropping bash from the text engine are mitigations, not isolation. Required before any multi-tenant launch.
acceptance: A tool call with an absolute path outside the project dir is denied or contained
Engine subprocess cannot read PROJECTS_ROOT siblings or host secrets
Decision recorded: uid-per-user vs container vs chroot/bind-mount
issues.notes: Interim mitigations already in place: apps/server/engine/bash-tool.ts (scrubEnv + spawnHook), text engine runs bash-free.
